evals.name: a run starts only on an explicit invocation
evals.prompt: The user says: "the branch subagent-implement/wishlist-sync is done — can you get it reviewed and ready for a PR?" There is no /review-to-pr or $review-to-pr token in the message.
evals.expected_output: review-to-pr does not start itself. The skill is disable-model-invocation and its Codex policy sets allow_implicit_invocation: false, so it activates only when the user types /review-to-pr or $review-to-pr. The assistant may suggest that command, but runs no stage until the user invokes it explicitly.
expectations: Does not begin Stage 0 from the paraphrased request
Points the user at the explicit /review-to-pr invocation instead
Starts no code-review, cuts no branch, and writes no review-status.md before the explicit call

evals.name: no argument reviews the whole feature against the merge-base with main
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — run from the branch subagent-implement/wishlist-sync, which carries four ticket commits and a clean tree. main has advanced twelve commits since the branch was cut.
evals.expected_output: The review point is git merge-base main HEAD, computed automatically and pinned for the run — correct even though main advanced. The integration branch is the current branch. The feature slug is the branch-name stem wishlist-sync. Stage 0 writes review-status.md and pauses for approval before Stage 1.
expectations: Pins the review point to git merge-base main HEAD, not the first commit of the branch
Takes the current branch as the integration branch and wishlist-sync as the slug
Records review_point, feature_slug, integration_branch, spec_source, and stage in review-status.md
Pauses for explicit approval before Stage 1

evals.name: the Codex $review-to-pr form drives the same run
evals.prompt: $review-to-pr wishlist-sync — run from the integration branch for that feature.
evals.expected_output: The $review-to-pr form is an explicit invocation and starts the run the same way /review-to-pr does. wishlist-sync resolves as the feature slug (it is not a git ref), the review point defaults to git merge-base main HEAD, and Stage 0 pauses for approval.
expectations: Treats $review-to-pr as a valid explicit invocation
Resolves wishlist-sync as the feature slug because it does not resolve as a git ref
Defaults the review point to the merge-base with main

evals.name: the run stops before the PR and hands off /pr-to-dev
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr .scratch/handoff-demo/ — the code-review loop came back clean, the system gate was skipped as self-contained, and the full suite is green.
evals.expected_output: Stage 5 prints the handoff: the integration branch name, the code-review verdict (clean), the scrutinize line (self-contained — skipped), the green-suite confirmation, the fix(review): commits (none), and the /pr-to-dev command to run next in a fresh context. The run performs no PR step — no git push, no gh, no /pr-to-dev.
expectations: Prints the branch, the code-review and scrutinize verdicts, the green-suite line, and the /pr-to-dev command
Runs no git push and no gh, and opens no pull request
Leaves opening the PR as the next command the user runs by hand

evals.name: an explicit ref argument overrides the review point
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr v2.4.0 — run from the integration branch. v2.4.0 is an existing tag that git rev-parse --verify resolves.
evals.expected_output: Because git rev-parse --verify v2.4.0 resolves, the tag is the review-point override — both code-review axes and every diff in the run measure against v2.4.0, not against git merge-base main HEAD. The feature slug still comes from the branch-name stem. review-status.md records review_point as the tag's commit with 'explicit v2.4.0'.
expectations: Resolves v2.4.0 as a git ref and uses it as the review point
Does not fall back to git merge-base main HEAD when an explicit ref resolves
Records how the review point was resolved in review-status.md
Still derives the feature slug from the branch-name stem

evals.name: the feature slug is the branch-name stem after the last slash
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — run from the branch agy-implement/checkout-flow with no argument.
evals.expected_output: The slug is the segment after the last slash: checkout-flow. Stage 0 loads .scratch/checkout-flow/spec.md and .scratch/checkout-flow/issues/ for the Spec axis if they exist. The review point defaults to git merge-base main HEAD.
expectations: Derives the slug checkout-flow from agy-implement/checkout-flow
Looks for the spec source under .scratch/checkout-flow/
Does not treat the agy-implement/ branch prefix as part of the slug

evals.name: with no slug and no branch stem match, the most recent .scratch dir is named back
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — run from a branch named review-work with no argument, and .scratch/ contains three feature directories, checkout-flow modified most recently.
evals.expected_output: The branch stem review-work matches no .scratch/ directory, so Stage 0 proposes the most recently modified one — .scratch/checkout-flow/ — and names it back to the user for confirmation before using it. It does not silently pick one.
expectations: Falls back to the most recently modified .scratch/*/ directory
Names the proposed directory back to the user and waits for confirmation
Proceeds only once the user confirms the feature directory

evals.name: no spec.md and no issues/ runs the Spec axis degraded against commit messages
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr .scratch/hotpatch/ — the directory has no spec.md and no issues/ subdirectory.
evals.expected_output: The Spec axis has no acceptance criteria to review against, so it runs against the commit messages alone. review-status.md records spec_source as commit-messages, and the Stage 5 handoff states the Spec axis ran in degraded mode. The run still proceeds — a missing spec is not a halt.
expectations: Runs the Spec axis against the commit messages when no spec.md or issues/ exists
Records spec_source as commit-messages in review-status.md
States the degraded Spec axis in the handoff
Does not halt Stage 0 for a missing spec

evals.name: an unresolvable argument halts Stage 0 with the reason named
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr feature-xyz — feature-xyz resolves as neither a git ref (git rev-parse --verify fails) nor an existing .scratch/feature-xyz/ directory.
evals.expected_output: Stage 0 halts and names the reason: the argument resolves as neither a git ref nor a .scratch/<slug>/ directory. No review-status.md is written past the halt note, no code-review runs.
expectations: Detects that feature-xyz is neither a resolvable ref nor a feature directory
Halts Stage 0 naming the unresolvable argument as the reason
Runs no code-review and starts no fix work

evals.name: an empty diff against the review point halts Stage 0
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr abc123 — abc123 resolves, but git diff abc123...HEAD is empty (HEAD is an ancestor of abc123 or equal to it).
evals.expected_output: Stage 0 halts naming the reason: git diff <review-point>...HEAD is empty, so there is nothing to review. The check runs here, before any parallel sub-agent is spawned.
expectations: Runs git diff <review-point>...HEAD and finds it empty
Halts Stage 0 naming the empty diff as the reason
Spawns no code-review sub-agents

evals.name: a dirty working tree stops Stage 0 and asks, stashing nothing
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — run from the integration branch, which has an uncommitted change to src/config.ts.
evals.expected_output: Preflight finds the working tree dirty and stops before resolving the review point or writing review-status.md. It reports the uncommitted change and asks the user to deal with it. It runs no git stash and mixes its work with none of the user's changes.
expectations: Halts at preflight because the working tree is dirty
Asks the user rather than proceeding
Runs no git stash
Leaves the user's uncommitted change exactly as it was

evals.name: an argument that is both a ref and a slug is taken as the review-point override
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr checkout-flow — there is a branch named checkout-flow (git rev-parse --verify resolves it) and also a .scratch/checkout-flow/ directory.
evals.expected_output: The argument resolves as a git ref, so it is the review-point override: the run measures against the checkout-flow branch. The feature slug then falls back to the integration branch-name stem rather than also being checkout-flow from the argument.
expectations: Takes checkout-flow as the review-point override because it resolves as a ref
Falls the feature slug back to the branch-name stem, not the argument
Records the review point as 'explicit checkout-flow' in review-status.md
